methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OSH Cut is a bootstrapped robotics and manufacturing company founded by Caleb and Jacom Chamberlain with no prior external funding. The comparable universe consists of nine firms in the robotics and manufacturing sector: one public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. A narrow peer-set comparison—filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier companies—yielded fewer than three datapoints across all three filters, falling below the minimum threshold needed for reliable triangulation. While eight same-sector robotics peers exist, none satisfy the stringent stage and tier criteria required for defensible comparable-company analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the wide dispersion in robotics company valuations across development stages and business models.

Without applicable triangulation methods, a quantitative valuation range cannot be supported by the data provided. Establishing a credible estimate would require either: (i) securing financial metrics and recent funding rounds from the identified peer set; (ii) obtaining OSH Cut's own revenue, EBITDA, or unit economics; or (iii) identifying additional same-stage private comparables in robotics and manufacturing. The bootstrapped status and apparent pre-revenue stage present significant valuation challenges absent observable market transactions or internal operating data.
